findings.statement: Rank 1 in the convergence ranking. Strongly tumour-up in TCGA-KIRC paired RNA [gene=CA9; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=9.71]. Open Targets tractability: AB, PR and SM; labelled AB Advanced Clinical and SM Approved Drug. Drugs as returned: GIRENTUXIMAB PHASE_3, IODINE I 124 GIRENTUXIMAB PHASE_2, SULTHIAME PHASE_4, ETHOXZOLAMIDE WITHDRAWAL. UniProt Q16790: cell membrane / microvillus membrane, so it suits antibody and imaging use. Reactome: HIF-regulated gene expression. DepMap: ccRCC lines do not depend on it (no dependent lines, not common essential), and it is not mutated (one patient of the cohort, not recurrent). It is therefore a surface-antigen and biomarker case, not a genetic-dependency case. PRISM: the most ccRCC-selective annotated compound is para-toluenesulfonamide, which has several targets, so it says little about CA9 itself [gene=CA9; type=prism_response; source=DATASET:PRISM-20Q2; selectivity=0.333].

Rank 4 in the convergence ranking. Strongly tumour-up in TCGA-KIRC [gene=CD70; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=7.09]. The tumour-intrinsic signal persists after purity adjustment. Tractability: AB and OC (both Advanced Clinical) and PR. Drugs as returned: CUSATUZUMAB PHASE_2, VORSETUZUMAB PHASE_1, VORSETUZUMAB MAFODOTIN PHASE_1, MDX-1411 PHASE_1. UniProt P32970: plasma membrane ligand of CD27. Reactome: TNF receptor binding. DepMap shows no ccRCC dependency and it is not common essential. This is an antibody or ADC antigen, not an intrinsic vulnerability. Its Open Targets association is low, so the evidence comes from expression and literature, not genetics.

Rank 30 in the convergence ranking. Tumour-up in TCGA-KIRC [gene=ENPP3; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=5.56]. Tractability: AB, OC (Advanced Clinical), PR and SM. Only drug returned: AGS-16C3F (an ADC) at PHASE_2. UniProt O14638: apical cell membrane and secreted, so it is accessible to antibodies and may be measurable as a soluble marker. DepMap shows no ccRCC dependency. It is a surface-antigen candidate that is tractable but only partly tested clinically. Open Targets association is low.

Established ccRCC drug target (HIF-2 alpha). Open Targets association score [gene=EPAS1; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.4871]. BELZUTIFAN is at APPROVAL, with SM tractability including Approved Drug. Reactome: HIF regulation, hypoxia response, PD-L1 transcription. It is the only top-ranked gene with a DepMap signal in ccRCC lines: more dependent than other lines [gene=EPAS1; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; selectivity=0.3]. About a fifth of ccRCC lines are dependent, the BH q-value is borderline, and it is not common essential. It sits outside the convergence top 25, with a wide robustness interval because RNA differential expression is modest. Its value rests on genetics, dependency and an approved drug, not on expression. PRISM cannot capture belzutifan-type biology in 2D culture.

Top Open Targets association with ccRCC, and the founding driver. Somatic recurrence in the CPTAC plus TCGA cohort [gene=VHL; type=somatic_recurrence; source=DATASET:SOMATIC-CPTAC-TCGA; freq=0.483]. The tumour-suppressor loss is a ccRCC-defining event, with frequent copy-number loss in the cohort. DepMap shows ccRCC lines are not selectively dependent on VHL: it is a loss-of-function driver, so it is not directly targetable. Its relevance is as the upstream cause of HIF-2 alpha activation, and so of CA9 and the other HIF-target biomarkers. Drug list is empty in the ranking.

Rank 8 in the convergence ranking, with the strongest biomarker profile among up-regulated genes. It is tumour-up with a purity-robust signal, and higher expression is associated with worse survival in TCGA (BH-significant). Open Targets lists no drug and only predicted tractability. DepMap does not support dependency: ccRCC lines are, if anything, less dependent than other lines. It is a prognostic and diagnostic marker candidate, not a validated target.

Rank 17 in the convergence ranking. It is tumour-up with a purity-robust signal and has predicted small-molecule tractability, but Open Targets returns no clinical drug. It is a plasma-membrane lactate transporter (MCT4) in the HIF glycolytic programme. DepMap shows no selective dependency in ccRCC lines (no dependent lines) and PRISM has no compound annotated to it. Druggability without dependency makes this a weaker target case. It remains of interest as a mechanism-linked candidate.

Rank 6 in the convergence ranking and the only top-10 gene combining tumour-up expression with a genetic Open Targets association (among the disease's leading Open Targets associations). Protein is also up in tumours. It is a membrane receptor (HDL/cholesterol uptake) with predicted tractability and no clinical drug returned. DepMap shows no ccRCC-selective dependency. It is an association-plus-expression candidate; its therapeutic value is untested.

Rank 3 in the convergence ranking. It is strongly down-regulated in tumours (loss of proximal tubule identity), and low expression is associated with worse survival in TCGA (BH-significant). Open Targets lists no drug. A down-regulated marker like this is useful for diagnosis and prognosis but cannot be targeted by inhibition. DepMap does not suggest dependency.

Rank 2 in the convergence ranking. It is strongly tumour-up in RNA and protein, with a purity-robust signal. Drugs listed (ME-344 PHASE_1_2; metformin entries at WITHDRAWAL) are non-specific mitochondrial or metabolic agents and are not evidence for selective targeting. Open Targets association is low, and DepMap shows no ccRCC dependency. It is a candidate tumour marker with little target support.

caveats: Open Targets scores for the established drivers (VHL, PBRM1, KDM5C, BAP1, SETD2) are high but these are loss-of-function tumour suppressors that cannot be inhibited directly; only VHL was checked for recurrence and DepMap here.
Most top-ranked genes by convergence are tumour-up surface or metabolic genes with no DepMap dependency. DepMap and PRISM use 2D cell lines and miss HIF-2 and microenvironment biology.
Drug stages are exactly as returned by Open Targets; antibody and ADC stages are not specific to ccRCC indications.
Down-regulated genes (ALDOB, SLC22A8, UMOD, FABP1) are biomarker candidates only. Convergence rank partly reflects literature counts, which favour well-studied genes.

The PubMed connector was not available (authorisation needed), so no independent literature check was done. STRING interactions were not queried and no per-gene pathway analysis was made beyond Reactome annotations.
Several candidates (SLC22A6, SLC22A8, SLC34A1, PIGR) in the top 25 were not profiled individually because of the tool-call budget.
